questions.hint: Is 저 the topic, the subject or the object? And does 저 end in a vowel or a consonant?
questions.note: 저 (I) is the topic of the sentence, so it takes the topic particle 은/는. 저 ends in a vowel, so it is 는. 은 is the same particle but used after a consonant, like 선생님은. 이 marks the subject and 를 marks the object, so they do not fit here.

questions.hint: Which particle goes with 있어요 (there is / to have)? Does 책 end in a vowel or a consonant?
questions.note: 있어요 (there is / to have) takes the subject particle 이/가 for the thing you have. 책 ends in a consonant (ㄱ), so it is 이. After a vowel it is 가, like 친구가 있어요 (I have a friend). 를 is wrong because 있어요 does not take an object.

questions.hint: Water is the thing you drink, so it is the object. Does 물 end in a vowel or a consonant?
questions.note: 마셔요 (drink) needs an object: what do you drink? Objects take 을/를. 물 ends in a consonant (ㄹ), so it is 을. After a vowel it is 를, like 커피를 마셔요.

questions.hint: Coffee is the thing you like, so it is the object. Does 커피 end in a vowel or a consonant?
questions.note: 좋아해요 (to like) takes an object with 을/를. 커피 ends in a vowel, so it is 를. Be careful: the similar word 좋아요 (is good) takes 이/가 instead, as in 커피가 좋아요.

questions.hint: You are going somewhere. Which particle marks where you are going?
questions.note: With verbs of movement like 가요 (go) and 와요 (come), 에 marks where you are going. The other options are wrong forms after a vowel: it would be 가, 는 and 와, and they do not mean "to" anyway.

questions.hint: Studying is an action. Which particle marks the place where an action happens?
questions.note: 공부해요 (study) is an action, so the place where it happens takes 에서. 에 is for where you go or where something is, as in 도서관에 가요 (I go to the library).

questions.hint: Does 사과 end in a vowel or a consonant?
questions.note: 사과 (apple) ends in a vowel, so "to be" is 예요. 이에요 is used after a consonant. 있어요 means "there is" and 해요 means "do", so they do not fit.

questions.hint: Does 선생님 end in a vowel or a consonant?
questions.note: 선생님 ends in a consonant (ㅁ), so "to be" is 이에요. 예요 is only used after a vowel, as in 의사예요 (I am a doctor).

questions.prompt: Which is the polite present tense?
questions.hint: The stem is 가. Its vowel is ㅏ, so which ending does it take, and what happens when two ㅏ meet?
questions.note: Remove 다 to get the stem 가. Its vowel is ㅏ, so you add 아요. Two ㅏ in a row merge into one, so 가 + 아요 becomes 가요, not 가아요. 갔어요 is the past tense (I went).

questions.prompt: Which is the polite past tense?
questions.hint: The stem is 먹. Is its vowel ㅏ or ㅗ, or something else?
questions.note: Remove 다 to get the stem 먹. Its vowel is ㅓ, not ㅏ or ㅗ, so the past tense ending is 었어요: 먹 + 었어요 = 먹었어요. 먹았어요 is wrong because 았어요 is only used after ㅏ or ㅗ. 먹어요 is present tense and 먹을 거예요 is future.
